text:
elaine: FYI customers in eu-west seeing p95/p99 spike since ~11:03 UTC, sudden TLS + connect time increases. Affected route: api.redwood-eu -> backend pool. p95 jumped 180ms -> 1.1s. p99 up to 2.3s. Metrics: https://dash/redwood/edge/route/eu-west (shortlink)
sam: Customer ticket #4521 reporting timeouts and slow completions. They attached curl showing long TCP/TLS handshake: 
```
$ curl -v https://api.redwood.com/complete -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...'
* Connected to api.redwood.com (54.77.x.x) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake completed in 820 ms
> GET /complete HTTP/1.1
```
ryan: I see a small increase in route churn in BGP for the eu-west pop around the same time. Not huge but some flapping between two upstreams. Can you run a traceroute from a failing probe? @nora can you check peering side?
elaine: pasted traceroute from synthetic probe located in fr-paris region: 
```
traceroute to api.redwood-eu (54.77.x.x), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.0.0.1  0.3 ms  0.2 ms  0.2 ms
 2  93.184.216.1  1.2 ms  0.9 ms  1.0 ms
 3  * * *
 4  203.0.113.5  120.5 ms  121.0 ms  119.8 ms
 5  54.77.x.x  121.3 ms  122.0 ms  121.6 ms
```
elaine: hop 3 is where we sometimes see transit provider blackhole/queueing — that 120ms jump is suspicious.
nora: Confirmed on peering dashboard: upstream-2 started engineering maintenance at 11:00 UTC but marked as maintenance; however we had partial failover to upstream-3 with asymmetric egress. I'll pull BGP updates.
ops-bot: incident:create id=INC-2026-382345 - "eu-west TLS p99 increase" severity=high
sam: Quick remediation idea: can we route customers on affected routes to dedicated fallback pool in the region (lower throughput but stable) to avoid long TLS handshakes? That would reduce p99 while infra investigates.
ryan: We can add a temporary routing policy to prefer upstream-1 (stable) for the eu-west pop and disable learned routes from upstream-2. Applying now — will monitor.
ops-bot: deploy:route-change eu-west prefer=upstream-1 by ryan at 11:14 UTC
elaine: after policy change p95 dropped to ~240ms, p99 to ~520ms within 90s. Customer on ticket confirms improvement. Still seeing occasional TLS handshake spikes ~500ms but much better than before.
sam: Any root cause hypothesis? Maintenance window + BGP flap + asymmetric path causing TLS handshake resends? Also looks like increased SYN retransmit rate in VPC logs.
nora: Peering log shows partial RPKI validation issue on upstream-2 causing them to withdraw some prefixes intermittently during their maintenance, which caused route oscillation. Their maintenance team acknowledged and rolled back a config at 11:12 UTC, but we still saw instability until we forced prefer-upstream-1.
ryan: Follow-ups: 1) add short-circuit to route preference when p95 exceeds threshold for more than 30s, 2) add synthetic handshake-time probe to detect upstream handshake inflation earlier, 3) notify account teams for customers with strict latency SLOs. I'll open a postmortem ticket.
elaine: Thanks team. Sam, keep customer ticket updated: described mitigation and ETA for full fix (monitoring for 4h). Closing this thread in ~1h if no regressions. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: incident:update id=INC-2026-382345 status=mitigated note="temporary route preference applied; monitoring"
